title: Samsung's Fluid AI design could be the blueprint for One UI 10's major visual overhaul
excerpt: A leaked banner suggests One UI 10 could bring Samsung’s biggest visual refresh yet.

Published Nov 18, 2026, 12:56 PM EST

Samsung could be preparing a major visual overhaul for One UI 10, which is expected to launch in 2027. In an X post, well-known tipster Ice Universe shared a leaked One UI 10 banner found in One UI 9.5 firmware, showing a translucent number 10 with a frosted-glass finish and a blurred lower edge. He also pointed out its similarities to Samsung’s award-winning Fluid AI Design system, fueling speculation about a possible redesign.

Ice Universe went a step further by sharing images of the Fluid AI concept alongside the leaked One UI 10 graphic. The examples show translucent panels, softly blurred backgrounds, rounded interface elements, and floating cards that present information such as notifications, calendar entries, and location details. The overall aesthetic is noticeably different from the more conventional interface elements found in current One UI versions.

One UI 10 could take inspiration from Samsung’s Fluid AI concept

The design focuses on more adaptive interfaces

Samsung’s Fluid AI Design System is a generative user interface concept that uses AI agents to interpret user interactions and contextual signals in real time. Rather than relying on fixed screens and predefined interaction rules, it envisions interfaces that adapt their appearance and position according to the user’s needs and surroundings.

Samsung confirmed that the Fluid AI Design System was among six AI-focused design concepts recognized at the 2026 Red Dot Design Awards. The recognition highlights that Samsung is exploring alternative approaches to how people interact with digital interfaces, although it doesn’t mean the concept is ready for commercial use.

Interfaces adapt their appearance and position according to the user’s needs and surroundings.

The similarities between the leaked graphic and the Fluid AI concept are hard to ignore. Both point towards a design language built around translucent elements and blurred backgrounds. If Samsung adopts some of these ideas for One UI 10, Galaxy phones could get a noticeably different visual identity.

For now, this remains speculation based on Ice Universe’s observations and the leaked firmware graphic. Samsung hasn’t announced One UI 10’s design direction or confirmed that Fluid AI will influence the update. One UI 10 is also expected to be based on Android 18 and could debut on the Galaxy Z Fold 9, which is rumored to launch around July 2027. Still, the two sets of visuals offer an interesting glimpse of what a future Galaxy interface could look like if Samsung decides to take a more experimental approach.
